about: Field-level guidance for workflows an AI writes with save_workflow (src/workflow-authoring-guidance.mjs). `fields` puts plain-words guidance on the fields of save_workflow's input schema (src/workflow-recipe-input.mjs): each row's `schema_path` is the list of keys from the schema's root to that field's schema, and `says` becomes its description, so an AI reading the tool sees how to fill each field before it writes one. `notes` are what a saved workflow is checked for after its write: none refuses a save; each that applies is returned under authoring_notes with the field it is about, so the author improves the workflow while it is still in hand. Note kinds the module reads: `longer_than` (a text at `at` over `chars` characters; `*` in `at` means every item of a list), `input_not_declared` (a binding reads ['input', name] that input_schema does not declare, so no run can give it), `literal_could_bind` (a tool step gives a literal value for an input the workflow's own input_schema declares, so every run would reuse this run's value), `tool_input_missing` (a tool step gives no value for an input its tool requires, so the run asks for it every time). Every word is under `says`.

fields.says: Short name, an action then its object ("Review a pull request"), at most 60 characters.
What the workflow gets done in plain words, at most 200 characters; find_workflow matches it, so name the job, never this run's values.

JSON Schema with type object for the workflow input. Declare every value a run must give (each one a step reads with ["input", name]) and mark those it cannot run without as required, so a start carries every input it needs.
Generic step name, at most 50 characters ("Fetch the open issues"), never a value of one run, so another person's question can run the same step.

What this step does, referring to values by where they come from (the workflow input, an earlier step), never by this run's values. Keep fetching in steps; how to group, rank or word the final answer belongs in the last step's do, not in extra steps.
JSON Schema with type object for what the step hands back; require the fields later steps and checks read.

For a step a Marketplace tool does: { tool_id, input }. Give fixed values only for what never changes; take everything else at run time with { "from": path } (first value) or { "all_from": path } (every value), from ["input", name] or ["steps", <earlier step id>, ...]. To run a tool once per item of an earlier result, write the workflow as a definition with a loop step. pinned is filled in when saved: the tool version the step was written for.

Instead of ordered steps, the engine step graph: asks, checks, and loops. A loop { id, kind: "loop", config: { definition_id: "workflow:<a saved workflow run per item>", source: { "$kind": "binding", "select": { "from": "start", "path": "input.items" } }, item_var: "item", max_iterations } } maps one workflow over every item of a list.

notes.says: label is longer than 60 characters; keep it an action and its object.
job is longer than 200 characters; say the job, and keep how it is done in the steps.
A step title is longer than 50 characters; keep titles short and generic.
A step reads ["input", "{name}"], which input_schema does not declare, so no run can give it. Declare it in input_schema.properties (and required when the step cannot run without it).
Step {step_id} gives {tool_id} a fixed {name}, which the workflow's input also declares. Write { "from": ["input", "{name}"] } so every run gives its own.
Step {step_id} gives {tool_id} no {name}, which the tool requires, so every run stops to ask for it. Give it from the workflow input or an earlier step.
